beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Agentic AI 2026 explains why useful agents need more than an intelligent model.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The surrounding software turns model predictions into actions with real consequences.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book follows tools, memory, permissions, verification, and recovery as one engineering problem.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its argument is that autonomy needs boundaries matched to the work being delegated.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You will learn to compare agent designs through evidence, control, and total operational cost.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The later proposals matter because the earlier chapters establish how to judge them.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Imagine an agent helping with a customer’s request for a refund.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It reads a public page, then proposes returning the customer’s money.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Those operations need different permissions, even within the same task.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Permission to read should not silently become permission to pay.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The surrounding software must check each proposed action against its own rules.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This distinction makes the book’s question concrete: who controls the consequences?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book then compares ways to organize a sequence of uncertain decisions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An agent might alternate reasoning and action, or work from an explicit plan.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Verification adds another question: did the proposed step produce the intended result?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Memory preserves useful state, but also creates material that later decisions may trust.
